title: Virginia DJJ Data Questions/Updates
text:
Virginia DJJ Data Questions and Responses:
Questions about the disposition file:

The disposition file appears to have a small number of pure duplicates (850/370,000) and a somewhat larger population of duplicates across youth ID, case number, offense, and disposition (11,000/370,000). How should we interpret/treat this? It seems like one case could have multiple intakes and thus, multiple measures of days from intake to disposition – but for one offense ID

Response from Nina: One case can have multiple complaints (aka offenses) and each one of the offenses may have one or more dispositions. So yes, there can be multiple measures of days from intake to disposition. The field in our data system calls it the court ordered date since the word “disposition” can mean different things to different individuals. Follow up from phone call: I looked at the data in our data system and the duplicates are correct. For example, the youth may be given more than one type of court ordered condition and the PO may put a disposition for each specific type.

We seem to be missing description, days_int_to_cd, and court_disp_age for about half of the records in the file. Are these intake complaints without dispositions? Or how should we interpret this?

Response from Nina: Since the complaint is diverted the worker may not have entered a disposition. The disposition and intake decision are captured in two different fields.
Questions about the intake complaints file:
Missing data:

How should we interpret missing prior JJ complaint data? About 40% of all intake complaints records appear to have missing data in these columns

Response from Nina: Missing means the youth had no prior involvement across all offense types/severities. For the records that have 0 rather than blank, this means they had no type of prior for that field (for example, if prior felony is 0 it means they had no prior felonies). However, they youth may have had a different type of prior (based on the example, the youth may have had a prior misdemeanor).

We seem to be missing age (pet_age) for about 35% of all records in the intake complaints file – how should we interpret this?

Response from Nina: Not all complaints are petitioned. If the case is not petitioned the age will be missing. The percentage missing decreases to less than one percent when intake decision is taken into consideration.

It also appears that we have risk level, mental health flag, and other assessment information for only about 38% of all records in the intake complaints file.

Response from Nina: Not every youth gets a YASI at intake. The youth will usually get a YASI if they have a social history completed, if they are placed on probation, or if they are committed.

Should we use intake decision to create the diverted versus not diverted samples? Are these codes overwritten over time? If so, which intake decision codes belong in the diverted group (“UNSUCCESSFUL DIVERSION/PETITION FILED” (code of ‘18’), “SUCCESSFUL DIVERSION” (code of ‘20’), and “UNSUCCESSFUL DIVERSION/NO PETITION FILED” (code of ‘21’),“REQ’D TO PARTICIPATE-DIVERSION” (code of ‘7’)?)

Response from Nina: The only codes that are overwritten are the diversion intake decisions. ),“REQ’D TO PARTICIPATE-DIVERSION” means the youth has an open diversion plan. When the diversion plan is closed they are either changed to one of the unsuccessful codes or the successful code. You can see how we categorize the different intake decisions on page 18 of the Data Resource Guide, FY 2022.
New Questions

Could you walk us through the difference between CHINS, CHINSUP, and STATUS categories? Why are all three categories (CHINS, CHINSUP, STATUS) included in prior history, but only status included in current charge?

Response from Nina:
These definitions are from pages 4, 5, and 96 of the Data Resource Guide, FY 2022.
- CHINS: a child whose behavior, conduct, or condition presents or results in a serious threat to (i) the wellbeing and physical safety of that child or, (ii) if under the age of 14, the well-being and physical safety of another person. To meet the definition of CHINS, there must be a clear and substantial danger to the life or health of the child or another person, and the intervention of the court must be found to be essential to provide the treatment, rehabilitation, or services needed by the child or the child’s family. See § 16.1-228 of the Code of Virginia. - CHINSup: a child who (i) is habitually and without justification absent from school despite opportunity and reasonable effort to maintain school attendance, (ii) runs away from family or lawful custodian on more than one occasion, or (iii) escapes from or leaves a court-ordered residential placement without permission. See § 16.1-228 of the Code of Virginia.
In the file the Prior Other Status includes the following: - Other Status Offenses: In the appendix of the DRG you can find the offenses that are considered other status offenses. See below.
- Marijuana Status: As of FY 2022, the “Narcotics” offense category no longer includes marijuana possession offenses. These offenses are captured under the new VCC prefix, MRJ. Beginning in FY 2022, there are two “Marijuana” categories: delinquent marijuana offenses and status marijuana offenses.

How should we interpret FIPS codes of X71 and X21 (both associated with CSU 029)?

Response from Nina: X indicates that the code was expired. In this case both FIPS were part of CSU 29. Effective in FY 2019, Bland Co. (FIPS 021) and Giles Co. (FIPS 071) are part of CSU 27. 

Should we be using the Offense Type column or Delinquent/Status/Technical/Traffic flag to select complaints that are status-related? Or does it not matter?

Response from Nina: This is something that was included with the request. I believe it was categorized the same way the offenses are categorized on page 21 of the Data Resource Guide, FY 2022.

Do you all have a rule for excluding youth of certain ages from analysis (based on the assumption that it is likely a data entry error? e.g., ages of 0-4 or 25+?) Or are the ages accurate and reflect non-JJ involvement?

Response from Nina: I think it depends on the type of offense/ages. I would exclude “youth” 21 and over since those are most likely data entry errors. Depending on the offense category, the younger ages (0-4 years) may be accurate. For example, if it’s a CHINS complaint the child may actually be 0-4 years old. For the rest of the complaints it is most likely a data entry error. For the Data Resource Guide, our cut off for the intake section is 8 to 20 years old.
Questions about the caseload file:

Caseload file seems to have duplicates across youth ID (juvenile number) and offense number – how should we interpret this?

Response from Nina: The worker selects a caseload status and then associates one or more offenses with it. The youth’s status can change, for example, the youth may be placed on diversion and then abscond and then go back on diversion status. In this scenario, the youth would have two diversion statuses in the file since it counts the LOS for each status individually.

What is the best way to join the caseload file to the other files (without case number)?

Response from Nina: I would use the juvenile number and offense number both are unique to youth. The same offense number is not used for other youth who had the same offense.

We seem to be missing div_at_int and div_bey_90 for the vast majority of the records in the file (87%+). Are these intake complaints that were not diverted? Or how should we interpret this?

Response from Nina: It looks like if the offense(s) were not associated with a diversion caseload status and that is why it is blank. They may have a different workload status(es). For example, you can see the probation and parole workload statuses on page 97 of the DRG. Data entry practices for diversion caseload statuses may vary by CSU.
- Update since our call: I verified with the person that wrote the query. If the youth has the juvenile number and offense number filled in but the two diversion columns are blank. It means the youth had another type of caseload status (pre-Dispositional tracking, probation, parole, etc.) or they did not have any caseload statuses. So it is possible to have the number of days for the two diversion codes filled in and also have a blank row because they had another type of status. If we have to rerun the data we can change the rules to exclude the blanks.

Do youth get a YASI when they are diverted?

Response from Nina: It is not in the procedure but in practice it may vary. I would defer to Ms. McWilliams on the answer to this question.

Are the prior fields mutually exclusive?

Response from Nina: Certain fields will not overlap (e.g., prior felony and prior misdemeanor). The only field that may overlap with felony and misdemeanor is the “other status” category. Different reference tables are used to calculate these fields. There should not be a huge overlap but it is possible. We could probably add a field for the total number of priors (let me know if you want any exclusions) because that shouldn’t change the scope of the project/ what you already requested.

Current Internal Questions & Next Steps:

Language: complaint vs intake complaint vs intake case
For complaint-level analysis, I’ve created a unique complaint ID using juvenile_number and case_number
Other variables to categorize/group: intake decision (see table 3 on basic descriptives page), petitioner type (see table 4 on basic descriptives page), disposition type (see table 8 on basic descriptives page), offense description for status offenses (see table 7 on basic descriptives page)
Do we want to include the following intake decisions/types in our base sample: “COMPLAINT UNFOUNDED”, “SHELTER CARE ONLY”, “RETURNED TO OUT-OF-STATE”, “REFERRED TO ANOTHER AGY FOR SV”, “RESOLVED”, “PENDING”? Look at DJJ-provided descriptions for these, as well.
Do we want to explore both CSU-level and region-level variation? (see: https://www.djj.virginia.gov/pages/community/court-service-units.htm)

    Intake Decision 
    Intake Decision Description 
    Prelim Intake Decision Grouping (for analysis) 
  
 

  
    PETITION FILED 
    A complaint was received, probable cause was established, and the offense decision was to file a petition. 
    Petitioned 
  
  
    PETITION/DETENTION ORDER FILED 
    A complaint was received, probable cause was established, and the offense decision was to file a petition and issue a detention order. 
    Petitioned 
  
  
    DETENTION ORDER ONLY 
    Detention order only issued for pre-dispositional cases. 
    Other 
  
  
    COURT SUMMONS 
    Law enforcement files a court summons directly with the court (e.g., traffic offenses, low-level alcohol/marijuana offenses). In some CSUs, the summons is then entered as a complaint using this offense decision. In other CSUs, the CSU never sees the summons. 
    Petitioned 
  
  
    PETITION/SHELTER CARE FILED 
    A complaint/affidavit was received and probable cause established. The juvenile requires placement outside the home and secure detention is not appropriate. 
    Petitioned 
  
  
    UNSUCCESSFUL DIVERSION/PETITION FILED 
    Offense decision on original complaint was to divert. Diversion contract was signed and juvenile violates diversion contract and decision was made (with supervisor approval) to void the diversion and file a petition on the offense. 
    Diverted 
  
  
    RESOLVED 
    A complaint was received and the issue was resolved at intake. 
    Resolved/Dismissed 
  
  
    SUCCESSFUL DIVERSION 
    The offense decision on an original complaint was to divert. Juvenile successfully completes all obligations of the diversion contract and the intake was closed. 
    Diverted 
  
  
    COMPLAINT UNFOUNDED 
    A complaint was received and probable cause could not be established. 
    Resolved/Dismissed 
  
  
    UNSUCCESSFUL DIVERSION/NO PETITION FILED 
    The offense decision on an original complaint was to divert. The diversion contract was signed and juvenile violates diversion contract; however, a petition was not filed. 
    Diverted 
  
  
    REFERRED TO ANOTHER AGY FOR SV 
    A complaint was received, probable cause was established, and the family was referred to another agency for services. 
    Diverted (Informal) 
  
  
    UNOFFICIAL COUNSELING-FAMILY C 
    A complaint was received and the intake officer recommended family counseling to the clients. Follow up by the intake officer is not required. 
    Diverted (Informal) 
  
  
    ACCEPTED VIA ICJ 
    Juvenile was accepted from another state for supervision. 
    Other 
  
  
    RETURNED TO PROBATION SUPERVIS 
    A complaint was received, probable cause was established, and the juvenile was already on probation for another offense. The juvenile will remain on probation and no new action will be taken. 
    Other 
  
  
    PENDING 
    A complaint was received and probable cause established. This code is for short-term use only. Generally, this is used when the intention is to divert and are awaiting the diversion appointment or when waiting for more information from the police department. 
    Other 
  
  
    SHELTER CARE ONLY 
    The juvenile was being sent to a non-secure facility or emergency shelter specifically approved to provide a range of as-needed services on an individual basis. See § 16.1-248.1 of the Code of Virginia for additional information. 
    Other 
  
  
    RETURNED TO OUT-OF-STATE 
    A complaint was received, the juvenile was under supervision in Virginia from another state, and the juvenile was returned to that state. 
    Other 
  
  
    REQ'D TO PARTICIPATE-DIVERSION 
    A complaint was received, probable cause was established, and the complaint was diverted. Diversion is the handling of a juvenile intake compliant in an informal manner rather than through the official court process. The intake officer must develop a plan for the juvenile that may include counseling, informal supervision, restitution, community service, or other programs. The juvenile and his/her parents must agree to the diversion plan. Informal supervision is limited to 90 days for truancy and 120 days for all other offenses. The following complaints may not be diverted: an alleged violent juvenile felony, a complaint after a prior diversion or adjudication on a felony offense, and a second or subsequent truancy complaint. See § 16.1-227 and 16.1- 260 of the Code of Virginia for additional information. 
    Diverted

#####################################
### first explore how mso_flag (which flags most serious offense per case) is created b/c this is 
### how we will de-dup the complaints file and DJJ noted that one case may have two offenses flagged as "Yes" with the mso_flag if the severity rankings tie
### looking at the df produced here, the severity hierarchy appears to be created using vcc code (The Virginia Crime Code of the offense) 
### so by de-duping using mso_flag, we won't lose any offense-level data
### since we are calculating case-level counts of offenses by each category, this de-duping strategy 
### seems good to go
######################################################################################################
df_djj_intake_complaints_raw_mso_flag_dups_explore <- df_djj_intake_complaints_raw %>% 
  dplyr::filter(mso_flag == "Y") %>% 
  group_by(juvenile_number,
           case_number,
           mso_flag) %>% 
  mutate(sequence = row_number(),
         dup_mso=n()>1) %>% 
  ungroup() %>% 
  filter(dup_mso==TRUE) %>% 
  dplyr::select(juvenile_number,
           case_number,
           offense_number,
           mso_flag,
           dup_mso,
           sequence,
           vcc_code,
           description,
           dai,
           flg_category)

########################################
### clean and de-dup caseload dataframe
### we will then join this file to the intake complaints file, before we de-dup the intake complaints file by case/complaint. b/c the caseload file only contains youth ID and offense ID as unique identifiers, we need to join to intake complaints when the full universe of offense IDs is still present
### we'll then group by case/complaint to create LOS measures, from caseload, for our analysis
### first, here is some caseload-specific cleaning we need to do
########################################

###############################################
### from Nina on missing values:

### "I verified with the person that wrote the query. If the youth has the juvenile number and offense number filled in but the two diversion columns are blank. It means the youth had another type of caseload status (pre-Dispositional tracking, probation, parole, etc.) or they did not have any caseload statuses. So it is possible to have the number of days for the two diversion codes filled in and also have a blank row because they had another type of status. If we have to rerun the data we can change the rules to exclude the blanks."

### BUSINESS RULE: based on this, I am dropping records with missing values for either div_at_int or div_bey_90
################################################

################################################
### from Nina on duplicate youth and offense IDs

### "The worker selects a caseload status and then associates one or more offenses with it. The youth’s status can change, for example, the youth may be placed on diversion and then abscond and then go back on diversion status. In this scenario, the  youth would have two diversion statuses in the file since it counts the LOS for each status individually."

### BUSINESS RULE: based on this, i think it's best to group by youth ID and offense ID, add up all LOS values, and then de-duplicate
#################################################

caseload_clean <- caseload %>% 
  filter(!is.na(div_at_int) | !is.na(div_bey_90)) %>% 
  mutate(div_at_int = as.numeric(div_at_int),
         div_bey_90 = as.numeric(div_bey_90)) %>% 
  group_by(juvenile_number,
           offense_number) %>% 
  mutate(div_at_int = sum(div_at_int, na.rm = TRUE),
         div_bey_90 = sum(div_bey_90, na.rm = TRUE)) %>% 
  ungroup() %>% 
  distinct(juvenile_number,
           offense_number,
           .keep_all=TRUE)

### clean and de-dup df_djj_intake_complaints_raw dataframe by complaint/case (keeping most serious offense)
### this is our base complaint/offense-level file for the sample
#############################################
df_djj_intake_complaints_clean <- df_djj_intake_complaints_raw %>% 
  distinct(juvenile_number,
           case_number,
           offense_number,
           .keep_all=TRUE) %>% ### no records dropped
  ### we need to join caseload_clean to the intake complaints file before we de-dup the intake complaints file by case/complaint (keeping most serious offense). b/c the caseload file only contains youth ID and offense ID as unique identifiers, we need to join to intake complaints when the full universe of offense IDs is still present
  ### we'll then group by case/complaint to create LOS measures, from caseload, for our analysis
    left_join(caseload_clean,
            by = c("juvenile_number",
                   "offense_number")) %>% 
  ### create counts vars by charge category before de-duping with mso_flag (keeping the most serious offense)
  group_by(juvenile_number,
           case_number) %>% 
  mutate(count_felony_with_case = n_distinct(offense_number[dai%in%c("Felony against Persons",
                                                                     "Felony Weapons and Felony Narcotics Distribution",
                                                                     "Other Felony")]),
         count_misd_with_case = n_distinct(offense_number[dai%in%c("Class 1 Misdemeanor Against Persons",
                                                                     "Other Class 1 Misdemeanor")]),
         count_status_with_case = n_distinct(offense_number[dai%in%c("Status Offense")]),
         count_violation_with_case = n_distinct(offense_number[dai%in%c("Other Violation",
                                                                        "Court Order Violation",
                                                                        "Prob./Parole Violation")]),
         div_at_int = sum(div_at_int, na.rm = TRUE),
         div_bey_90 = sum(div_bey_90, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  ungroup() %>% 
  ### keep most serious offense associated with intake case/complaint
  dplyr::filter(mso_flag == "Y") %>% 
  ### according to DJJ documentation, multiple offenses may have mso flag of 1 if
  ### severity ranking is tied; it appears that ties only occur with identical vcc codes
  ### but will confirm with Nina
  distinct(juvenile_number,
           case_number,
           .keep_all=TRUE) %>% 
  ### clean race/ethnicity and gender
  ### use factor function to assign labels to values
  mutate(race_clean = case_when(
    race=="I" & hispanic!="Y" ~ 1,
    race=="A" & hispanic!="Y" ~ 2,
    race=="B" & hispanic!="Y" ~ 3,
    hispanic=="Y" ~ 4,
    race=="W" & hispanic!="Y" ~ 5,
    race %in% c("X","O") & hispanic!="Y" ~ 6,
    TRUE ~ as.numeric(NA)),
    race_clean = factor(race_clean,
         levels = c(1,2,3,4,5,6),
         labels = c("American Indian","Asian", "Black", "Hispanic", "White", "Other"))) %>% 
  mutate(gender_clean = case_when(
    sex=="F" ~ 1,
    sex=="M" ~ 2,
    TRUE ~ as.numeric(NA)),
    gender_clean = factor(gender_clean,
         levels = c(1,2),
         labels = c("Female", "Male"))) %>% 
  ### temp cleaning of age -- pending feedback from DJJ
  mutate(petition_age_clean = case_when(
    pet_age < 12 ~ 1,
    pet_age>= 12 &  pet_age< 14 ~ 2,
    pet_age>= 14 &  pet_age< 16 ~ 3,
    pet_age>= 16 &  pet_age< 20 ~ 4,
    TRUE ~ as.numeric(NA)),
    petition_age_clean = factor(petition_age_clean,
         levels = c(1,2,3,4),
         labels = c("Less than 12", 
                    "12 to 13",
                    "14 to 15",
                    "16 to 20")),
    intake_age_clean = case_when(
    intake_age < 12 ~ 1,
    intake_age>= 12 &  intake_age< 14 ~ 2,
    intake_age>= 14 &  intake_age< 16 ~ 3,
    intake_age>= 16 &  intake_age< 20 ~ 4,
    TRUE ~ as.numeric(NA)),
    intake_age_clean = factor(intake_age_clean,
         levels = c(1,2,3,4),
         labels = c("Less than 12", 
                    "12 to 13",
                    "14 to 15",
                    "16 to 20")),
    risk_level_clean = case_when(
    risk_level=="L" ~ 1,
    risk_level=="M" ~ 2,
    risk_level=="H" ~ 3,
    TRUE ~ as.numeric(NA)),
    risk_level_clean = factor(risk_level_clean,
         levels = c(1,2,3),
         labels = c("Low", 
                    "Medium",
                    "High"))) %>%   
  ### clean dates and create year for potential grouping in future trend analysis
  mutate(date_opened = ymd(as_date(excel_numeric_to_date(as.numeric(as.character(date_opened)), 
                                                  date_system = "modern"))),
         ysai_date = ymd(as_date(ysai_date)),
         date_opened_year = year(date_opened)) %>% 
  ### remove records for youth/individuals younger than 8 and older than 20
  ### feedback from Nina on this business rule: 
  ### "I would exclude “youth” 21 and over since those are most likely data entry errors. 
  ### Depending on the offense category, the younger ages (0-4 years) may be accurate. 
  ### For example, if it’s a CHINS complaint the child may actually be 0-4 years old. 
  ### For the rest of the complaints it is most likely a data entry error. For the Data Resource Guide, 
  ### our cut off for the intake section is 8 to 20 years old
  filter((drg=="CHINS" | intake_age >=8),
         intake_age<=20)

   ### clean up petitioner type variable for csu-level analysis (with fewer categories)
  mutate(referral_source_clean_csu_level_categories = case_when(
    petitioner_desc%in%c("BASE POLICE","Other Law Enforcment","POLICE DEPARTMENT","SHERIFF","STATE POLICE","PROBATION OFFICER") ~ "Law Enforcement",
    petitioner_desc%in%c("SCHOOL OFFICIAL","School Res. Officer") ~ "School",
    petitioner_desc%in%c("CITIZEN","RELATIVE","SELF","SPOUSE","COURT","ABC BOARD","COMMONWLTHS ATTORNEY","COMMUNITY SRV BOARD","DETENTION HOME","FIRE DEPARTMENT","GROUP HOME","MENTAL HLTH OFFICIAL","MERCHANTS","NCIS","SOCIAL SERVICE") ~ "Other",
   TRUE ~ as.character(NA))) %>% 
  ### create var for jj history using flags provided by DJJ
   mutate(jj_history_clean = case_when(
    (is.na(prior_adj)==TRUE) | (prior_other==0 & prior_chinsup==0 & prior_chins==0 & prior_other_status==0 & prior_misd==0 & prior_felony==0) ~ "No Prior JJ History",
    prior_other>0 ~ "Prior 'Other' History",
    (prior_chinsup>0 | prior_chins>0 | prior_other_status>0) ~ "Prior Status/CHINS/CHINsup",
    prior_misd>0 ~ "Prior Misdemeanor",
    prior_felony>0 ~ "Prior Felony",
    TRUE ~ as.character(NA)),
    jj_history_clean = factor(jj_history_clean,
                              levels = c("No Prior JJ History","Prior 'Other' History","Prior Status/CHINS/CHINsup","Prior Misdemeanor","Prior Felony"))) %>% 
  mutate(csu_region = case_when(
    csu %in% eastern_region ~ "Eastern",
    csu %in% northern_region ~ "Northern",
    csu %in% western_region ~ "Western",
    csu %in% southern_region ~ "Southern",
    csu %in% central_region ~ "Central", 
    TRUE ~ as.character(NA))) %>% 
  ### now create recidivism-type variable for research question b in part I analysis:
  ### for youth who are diverted, how likely are they to come back into the system with a new complaint or new petition within a year of the initial intake decision? we are treating a new case_number as a new complaint (as opposed to a violation of an existing complaint/case)
  ### our outcome variable will be re-complaint within a year of the initial intake decision date (0/1)
  ### since the file is already distinct by complaint/case,
  ### now arrange and group by individual to take the next complaint/intake date, if present
  ### following a complaint's intake date using dplyr::lead to take the next start date
  ### after a given end date (https://dplyr.tidyverse.org/reference/lead-lag.html)
  ### this will allow us to calculate the average time from one complaint intake date to the next
  ### for youth who don't have any subsequent complaints in the sample, there will be an
  ### NA for next_complaint_intake_date  
  
  ### first, create date var for petitioned cases only (for second outcome of interest -- petitioned within a year of initial complaint)
  mutate(date_opened_petitioned_only = ifelse(intake_decision_clean=="Petitioned",
                                              as.character(date_opened),
                                              NA),
           date_opened_petitioned_only = ymd(as.Date(as.character(date_opened_petitioned_only)))) %>% 
  arrange(juvenile_number,
          case_number,
          date_opened) %>%
  group_by(juvenile_number) %>%
  mutate(next_complaint_intake_date = dplyr::lead(date_opened,
                                                   1,
                                                   default=NA),
         next_petition_intake_date = dplyr::lead(date_opened_petitioned_only,
                                                   1,
                                                   default=NA)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  ### now calculate time between the two intake dates in days and flag records with a subsequent complaint within a year
  mutate(time_between_complaints = as.numeric(difftime(next_complaint_intake_date,
                                                                    date_opened,
                                                                    units="days")),
         time_between_complaints_within_one_year_flag = ifelse(time_between_complaints<=365 & !is.na(time_between_complaints)==TRUE,
                                                             1,0),
         regression_outcome_new_complaint_one_year_first_time_jj = ifelse(time_between_complaints_within_one_year_flag==1 & jj_history_clean=="No Prior JJ History",
                                                             1,0),
         time_between_complaint_petition = as.numeric(difftime(next_petition_intake_date,
                                                                    date_opened,
                                                                    units="days")),
         time_between_complaint_petition_within_one_year_flag = ifelse(time_between_complaint_petition<=365 & !is.na(time_between_complaint_petition)==TRUE,
                                                             1,0),
         regression_outcome_new_petition_one_year_first_time_jj = ifelse(time_between_complaint_petition_within_one_year_flag==1 & jj_history_clean=="No Prior JJ History",
                                                             1,0))

#############################################
### clean and de-dup df_djj_intake_complaints_raw dataframe for complaints that are petitioned
### we will use this file ensure we only keep disposition data for complaints/cases that are actually petitioned
### here are the intake decisions that I am considering as "petitioned" -- meaning they should have disposition data:
### "PETITION FILED", "PETITION/DETENTION ORDER FILED","COURT SUMMONS","PETITION/SHELTER CARE FILED","UNSUCCESSFUL DIVERSION/PETITION FILED"
#############################################
df_djj_intake_petitioned_only <- df_complaints_youth_intake_decision %>%
  filter(intake_decision_label%in%c("PETITION FILED", "PETITION/DETENTION ORDER FILED","COURT SUMMONS","PETITION/SHELTER CARE FILED","UNSUCCESSFUL DIVERSION/PETITION FILED")) %>%

########################################
### clean and de-dup disposition dataframe
########################################
### note: disposition file is unique by youth, case number, offense number, disposition, and days from intake to disposition


### current hierarchy for de-duping disposition by severity:
# Commitment
# Detention
# Probation/Supervision
# Community Service
# Restitution
# Fine
# Other
# Deferral
# No further action/none

disposition_clean <- disposition %>% 
  ### remove records with missing disposition -- waiting on answer from DJJ on how to interpret this
  filter(!is.na(description)==TRUE) %>% 
  distinct(juvenile_number,
           case_number,
           offense_number,
           description,
           .keep_all=TRUE) %>% ### no records dropped
  ### create unique disposition ID for counts
  mutate(dispo_id = paste0(juvenile_number,
                           case_number,
                           offense_number,
                           description)) %>% 
  ### current options for grouping dispositions are: Detention, Commitment, Probation/Supervision, Deferral, Community Service, Fine, Treatment/Programming, No further action/none, Restitution, Other
  mutate(dispo_description_clean = case_when(
    description%in%c("COMMIT TO DJJ (16.1-278.8.14)","SERIOUS OFFENDER COMMITMENT TO DJJ (16.1-278.8.17) (16.1-285.1)") ~ 1,
    description%in%c("POST-DISPOSITIONAL DETENTION (16.1-278.8.16) (16.1-284.1)","SENTENCED TO DETENTION") ~ 2,
    description%in%c("COURT ORDER CONDITIONS AND LIMITATIONS (16.1-278.8.2)", "DEFER FINDING AND DISPOSITION W/PROBATION SUPERVISION (16.1-278.8.5)","PROBATION (16.1-278.8.7)","PROBATION AND COURT ORDERED ALCOHOL OR DRUG ABUSE TREATMENT (16.1-278.8.7a","(EXPIRED) DEFER DISPOSTION AND PLACE IN BOOT CAMP (16.1-278.8.4a)", "COURT ORDER GANG ACTIVITY PREVENTION PROGRAM (16.1-278.8.19)","FIRST OFFENSE DRUG VIOLATION, MANDATORY TREATMENT (16.1-278.8:01)","SUSPENDED COMMITMENT TO DJJ","SUSPENDED COMMITMENT TO DETENTION") ~ 3,
    description%in%c("COMMUNITY SERVICE (16.1-278.8.11)") ~ 4,
    description%in%c("RESTITUTION (16.1-278.8.10)") ~ 5,
    description%in%c("FINE NOT TO EXCEED $500 (16.1-278.8.8)") ~ 6,
    description%in%c("LOSS OF DRIVING PRIVS FOR ALCOHOL,FIREARM,OR TRUANCY(16.1-278.8.18)(16.1-278.9)","SENTENCED IN CIRCUIT COURT","SUSPEND DRIVER'S LICENSE/IMPOSE CURFEW (16.1-278.8.9)","TRAFFIC VIOLATION PENALTIES (16.1-278.8.12)","TRANSFER LEGAL CUSTODY (16.1-278.8.12)","UPHOLDING RULING OF THE LOWER COURT","(EXPIRED) TRANSFER TO CIRCUIT COURT","ADULT SENTENCED FOR JUVENILE OFFENSE (16.1-278.8.15) (16.1-284)","COURT ORDER NON-RESIDENTIAL PARENT PARTICIPATION IN PROGRAMS (16.1-278.8.6)","COURT ORDER PARENT PARTICIPATION IN PROGRAMS...FOR REHABILITATION (16.1-278.8.3)") ~ 7,
    description%in%c("DEFER DISPOSITION ON CONDITION OF GOOD BEHAVIOR") ~ 8,
    description%in%c("NO FURTHER ACTION") ~ 9,
   TRUE ~ as.numeric(NA))) %>% 
  ### use factor function to assign labels to values
  ### we'll use this to de-dup file and keep most severe disposition 
  mutate(dispo_description_clean = factor(dispo_description_clean,
         levels = c(1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8,9),
         labels = c("Commitment",
                    "Detention",
                    "Probation/Supervision",
                    "Community Service",
                    "Restitution",
                    "Fine",
                    "Other",
                    "Deferral",
                    "No further action/none"))) %>%
   ### create counts vars by disposition category before de-duping by case/complaint (keeping the most serious disposition)
  group_by(juvenile_number,
           case_number) %>% 
  mutate(count_commitment_dispo = n_distinct(dispo_id[dispo_description_clean=="Commitment"]),
         count_commitment_dispo = n_distinct(dispo_id[dispo_description_clean=="Detention"]),
         count_probation_supervision_dispo = n_distinct(dispo_id[dispo_description_clean=="Probation/Supervision"]),
         count_comm_service_dispo = n_distinct(dispo_id[dispo_description_clean=="Community Service"]),
         count_restitution_dispo = n_distinct(dispo_id[dispo_description_clean=="Restitution"]),
         count_fine_dispo = n_distinct(dispo_id[dispo_description_clean=="Fine"]),
         count_other_dispo = n_distinct(dispo_id[dispo_description_clean=="Other"]),
         count_deferral_dispo = n_distinct(dispo_id[dispo_description_clean=="Deferral"]),
         count_no_further_action_dispo = n_distinct(dispo_id[dispo_description_clean=="No further action/none"])) %>%
  ungroup() %>% 
  ### now order disposition by severity (by case_number)
  ### and keep record with most serious disposition based on above hierarchy
  arrange(juvenile_number,
          case_number,
          dispo_description_clean) %>% 
  distinct(juvenile_number,
           case_number,
           .keep_all = TRUE) %>% 
    ### temp cleaning of age -- pending feedback from DJJ
  mutate(dispo_age_clean = case_when(
    court_disp_age < 12 ~ 1,
    court_disp_age>= 12 &  court_disp_age< 14 ~ 2,
    court_disp_age>= 14 &  court_disp_age< 16 ~ 3,
    court_disp_age>= 16 &  court_disp_age< 20 ~ 4,
    TRUE ~ as.numeric(NA)),
    dispo_age_clean = factor(dispo_age_clean,
         levels = c(1,2,3,4),
         labels = c("Less than 12", 
                    "12 to 13",
                    "14 to 15",
                    "16 to 20"))) %>% 
  dplyr::rename(dispo_description = description) %>% 
  ### only keep disposition records with intake records/case IDs that were petitioned
  inner_join(df_djj_intake_petitioned_only,
             by = c("juvenile_number",
                    "case_number")) %>% 
  ### remove duplicated columns that we'll use from the intake complaints file
  dplyr::select(-offense_number)

### first, left join df_complaints_youth_intake_decision and disposition_clean
### we have already dropped disposition records without accompanying intake records which were petitioned
### so any disposition missingness indicates that case wasn't petitioned

### also: because we have already de-duped both df_complaints_youth_intake_decision (keeping most serious offense per case/complaint) and disposition_clean (keeping most serious disposition per case/complaint), we can just join by case/complaint as opposed to charge

                                               disposition_clean,

title: Analysis: Part I
text:
Research Questions:
Using a cohort of first-time system involved youth, look at adjusted differences in likelihood of being diverted and likelihood of a re-complaint for diverted vs. non-diverted youth.
A. How does the likelihood of being diverted differ by race, sex, and geography?
B. For youth who are diverted, how likely are they to come back into the system with a new complaint or new petition within a year of the initial intake decision?

Methods:
For research question (A) we will build a series of logistic regression models, adjusting for race/ethnicity, age, offense, risk level, and other factors that may also be related to a decision to divert. Our outcome variable will be diversion/petition (0/1) and our independent variables of interest will be race, sex, and CSU. For research question (B) we will take a similar methodological approach, but restrict our cohort to diverted youth and focus on likelihood of a re-complaint within a year of diversion while adjusting for demographics, offense, risk level, etc. For research question (B) our outcome variable will be re-complaint within a year of the initial intake decision date (0/1) and our independent variables of interest will be race, sex, and CSU.
Cohort: first time system involved youth (no prior complaints), 2016-2021
Method: Logistic Regression, which allows us to look at the relationship between two variables (like race and decision to divert) while adjusting for other factors that may also be related to our outcome (like offense, risk, etc.).

title: Part II Analysis: Race/Ethnicity
text:
Data Sample:
Research Question:
Conduct a front-end system assessment from intake through petition for all complaints 2016-2021.
Methods:
We will conduct a descriptive analysis of the front end of the system from intake through petition, provide unadjusted counts, RRI’s and means tests where applicable, by race, sex, offense, risk, CSU, and year for:
Cohort: All complaints from 2016-2021

title: Analysis: Part I
text:
Research Questions:
Using a cohort of first-time system involved youth, look at adjusted differences in likelihood of being diverted and likelihood of a re-complaint for diverted vs. non-diverted youth.
A. How does the likelihood of being diverted differ by race, sex, and geography?
B. For youth who are diverted, how likely are they to come back into the system with a new complaint or new petition within a year of the initial intake decision?

Methods:
For research question (A) we will build a series of logistic regression models, adjusting for race/ethnicity, age, offense, risk level, and other factors that may also be related to a decision to divert. Our outcome variable will be diversion/petition (0/1) and our independent variables of interest will be race, sex, and CSU. For research question (B) we will take a similar methodological approach, but restrict our cohort to diverted youth and focus on likelihood of a re-complaint within a year of diversion while adjusting for demographics, offense, risk level, etc. For research question (B) our outcome variable will be re-complaint within a year of the initial intake decision date (0/1) and our independent variables of interest will be race, sex, and CSU.
Cohort: first time system involved youth (no prior complaints), 2016-2021
Method: Logistic Regression, which allows us to look at the relationship between two variables (like race and decision to divert) while adjusting for other factors that may also be related to our outcome (like offense, risk, etc.).

title: Analysis: Part I
text:
Research Questions:
Using a cohort of first-time system involved youth, look at adjusted differences in likelihood of being diverted and likelihood of a re-complaint for diverted vs. non-diverted youth.
A. How does the likelihood of being diverted differ by race, sex, and geography?
B. For youth who are diverted, how likely are they to come back into the system with a new complaint or new petition within a year of the initial intake decision?

Methods:
For research question (A) we will build a series of logistic regression models, adjusting for race/ethnicity, age, offense, risk level, and other factors that may also be related to a decision to divert. Our outcome variable will be diversion/petition (0/1) and our independent variables of interest will be race, sex, and CSU. For research question (B) we will take a similar methodological approach, but restrict our cohort to diverted youth and focus on likelihood of a re-complaint within a year of diversion while adjusting for demographics, offense, risk level, etc. For research question (B) our outcome variable will be re-complaint within a year of the initial intake decision date (0/1) and our independent variables of interest will be race, sex, and CSU.
Cohort: first time system involved youth (no prior complaints), 2016-2021
Method: Logistic Regression, which allows us to look at the relationship between two variables (like race and decision to divert) while adjusting for other factors that may also be related to our outcome (like offense, risk, etc.).

title: ezapop_jj_base_clean_sas
text:
Purpose of syntax: To create a county-level juvenile population lookup table w/ race/ethnicity and gender for state of interest. The American Community Survey does not publicly report out population estimates for youth 10-17 (or 10-16 when relevant) at the county level and disaggregated by race/ethnicity and gender. Instead, I am pulling from Census Bureau ACS data provided to the CDC/National Center for Health Statistics which provides single year-of-age- estimate at the county level “to meet programmatic needs such as the creation of age groupings that differ from the standard groupings used by the Census Bureau.” This is also the source used by Ezapop, which was developed by OJJDP and NCJJ: https://www.ojjdp.gov/ojstatbb/ezapop/asp/source.asp
Because of concerns about reliability of single year-of-age estimates at the county-level, I am grouping age together (usually 10-17) and pulling estimates from 5 years of data (taking the mean across the five years), 2015-2019

### pull in raw sas files from: https://www.cdc.gov/nchs/nvss/bridged_race/data_documentation.htm#vintage2019
### file documentation here: https://www.cdc.gov/nchs/nvss/bridged_race/Documentation-BridgedPostcenV2019.pdf
### NOTE: we're pulling 5 years of data and then averaging across all files -- this is the approach that the american community survey takes for making more reliable estimates at the county/tract level (see more explanation/rationale here: https://www.census.gov/programs-surveys/acs/guidance/estimates.html)

### soft code state for easy substitution of new states, using fips code (e.g. indiana is 18, michigan is 26, etc.)
state_to_pull <- 51
  
# svDialogs::dlg_input(message = "Enter state FIPS code", default = "")$res

### soft code state abbreviation for easy substitution into file output name
state_name_abbr <- "va"
  
# svDialogs::dlg_input(message = "Enter state abbreviation", default = "")$res

### pull 2019 flat file
df_acs_bridged_age_race_sex_19 <- haven::read_sas("C:\\Users\\abyrum\\The Council of State Governments\\JC Research - JJ_Indiana - JJ_Indiana\\Data\\Syntax\\ezapop_raw_data_file\\pcen_v2019_y19.sas7bdat") %>% 
  zap_label() %>%  ### remove sas column labels 
  clean_names() %>% 
  filter(st_fips == as.numeric(state_to_pull)) ### this is where we filter on state

### pull 2018 flat file
df_acs_bridged_age_race_sex_18 <- haven::read_sas("C:\\Users\\abyrum\\The Council of State Governments\\JC Research - JJ_Indiana - JJ_Indiana\\Data\\Syntax\\ezapop_raw_data_file\\pcen_v2019_y18.sas7bdat") %>% 
  zap_label() %>%  ### remove sas column labels 
  clean_names() %>% 
  filter(st_fips == as.numeric(state_to_pull)) ### this is where we filter on state

### pull 2017 flat file

  zap_label() %>%  ### remove sas column labels 
  clean_names() %>% 
  filter(st_fips == as.numeric(state_to_pull)) ### this is where we filter on state

### pull 2016 flat file

### combine all five years for averaging -- stacking all five dataframes together
### documentation for race, ethnicity, sex recoding:
### racesex: 1=White male; 2=White female; 3=Black male; 4=Black female; 5=American Indian or Alaska Native male; 6=American Indian or Alaska Native female; 7=Asian or Pacific Islander male; 8=Asian or Pacific Islander female
### hisp: 1=not Hispanic or Latino; 2=Hispanic or Latino

df_acs_bridged_age_race_sex_15_19_raw <- dplyr::bind_rows(df_acs_bridged_age_race_sex_15,df_acs_bridged_age_race_sex_16,df_acs_bridged_age_race_sex_17,df_acs_bridged_age_race_sex_18,df_acs_bridged_age_race_sex_19) %>% 
  filter(age<18 & age>=8) %>% ### filter file off juvenile base population of interest -- youth ages 8 to 17 
  mutate(racesex = factor(racesex,
         levels = c(1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8),
         labels = c("white_male", "white_female", "black_male", "black_female","am_in_ak_native_male","am_in_ak_native_female","asian_pi_male","asian_pi_female")),
         hisp = factor(hisp,
         levels = c(1,2),
         labels = c("not_hispanic", "hispanic"))) %>% ### use factor function to assign labels to values)  ### use factor function to assign labels to values
  dplyr::select(-c(race4,vintage,st_fips,month))


### average pop totals across ages and years, rounding to nearest whole number
df_acs_bridged_age_race_sex_15_19_grouped <- df_acs_bridged_age_race_sex_15_19_raw %>%
  group_by(co_fips,hisp,racesex) %>% ### group by co_fips, hisp, and racesex to group across age and year
  summarise(pop = round(sum(pop)/5, digits = 0)) %>% ### sum across ages and years divided by 5 years of data to reach mean 10-17 population per year from 2015-2019
  ungroup()

`summarise()` has grouped output by 'co_fips', 'hisp'. You can override using
the `.groups` argument.

### pivot stacked dataframe wide by age, year, and co_fips to see all race, ethnicity, and sex breakdowns by county, year, and age to sum across subgroups
df_acs_bridged_age_race_sex_15_19_wide <- df_acs_bridged_age_race_sex_15_19_grouped %>% 
  pivot_wider(names_from = c(hisp,racesex), values_from = pop) %>% 
  mutate(state = paste0(state_name_abbr))

### combine race and sex columns into several new overall columns for race/ethnicity overall, race overall w/o ethnicity, and sex overall
df_acs_bridged_age_race_sex_15_19_final <- df_acs_bridged_age_race_sex_15_19_wide %>% 
  mutate(not_hispanic_white = not_hispanic_white_male + not_hispanic_white_female,
         not_hispanic_black = not_hispanic_black_male + not_hispanic_black_female,
         not_hispanic_am_in_ak_native = not_hispanic_am_in_ak_native_male + not_hispanic_am_in_ak_native_female,
         not_hispanic_asian_pi = not_hispanic_asian_pi_male + not_hispanic_asian_pi_female,
         hispanic_white = hispanic_white_male + hispanic_white_female,
         hispanic_black = hispanic_black_male + hispanic_black_female,
         hispanic_am_in_ak_native = hispanic_am_in_ak_native_male + hispanic_am_in_ak_native_female,
         hispanic_asian_pi = hispanic_asian_pi_male + hispanic_asian_pi_female,
         hispanic_any_race = hispanic_white + hispanic_black + hispanic_am_in_ak_native + hispanic_asian_pi,
         overall_white = not_hispanic_white + hispanic_white,
         overall_black = not_hispanic_black + hispanic_black,
         overall_am_in_ak_native = not_hispanic_am_in_ak_native + hispanic_am_in_ak_native,
         overall_asian_pi = not_hispanic_asian_pi + hispanic_asian_pi,
         overall_male = not_hispanic_white_male + not_hispanic_black_male + not_hispanic_am_in_ak_native_male + not_hispanic_asian_pi_male + hispanic_white_male + hispanic_black_male + hispanic_am_in_ak_native_male + hispanic_asian_pi_male,
         overall_female = not_hispanic_white_female + not_hispanic_black_female + not_hispanic_am_in_ak_native_female + not_hispanic_asian_pi_female + hispanic_white_female + hispanic_black_female + hispanic_am_in_ak_native_female + hispanic_asian_pi_female,
         overall_8_17_population = overall_male + overall_female) %>% 
  dplyr::select(co_fips,overall_8_17_population,overall_female,overall_male,overall_asian_pi,overall_am_in_ak_native,overall_black,overall_white,hispanic_asian_pi,hispanic_am_in_ak_native,hispanic_black,hispanic_white,hispanic_any_race,not_hispanic_asian_pi,not_hispanic_am_in_ak_native,not_hispanic_black,not_hispanic_white)

### aggregate to state level
### combine race and sex columns into several new overall columns for race/ethnicity overall, race overall w/o ethnicity, and sex overall
df_acs_bridged_age_race_sex_15_19_final_state_agg <- df_acs_bridged_age_race_sex_15_19_wide %>% 
  group_by(state) %>% 
  summarize(not_hispanic_white = sum(not_hispanic_white_male + not_hispanic_white_female),
         not_hispanic_black = sum(not_hispanic_black_male + not_hispanic_black_female),
         not_hispanic_am_in_ak_native = sum(not_hispanic_am_in_ak_native_male + not_hispanic_am_in_ak_native_female),
         not_hispanic_asian_pi = sum(not_hispanic_asian_pi_male + not_hispanic_asian_pi_female),
         hispanic_white = sum(hispanic_white_male + hispanic_white_female),
         hispanic_black = sum(hispanic_black_male + hispanic_black_female),
         hispanic_am_in_ak_native = sum(hispanic_am_in_ak_native_male + hispanic_am_in_ak_native_female),
         hispanic_asian_pi = sum(hispanic_asian_pi_male + hispanic_asian_pi_female),
         hispanic_any_race = sum(hispanic_white + hispanic_black + hispanic_am_in_ak_native + hispanic_asian_pi),
         overall_white = sum(not_hispanic_white + hispanic_white),
         overall_black = sum(not_hispanic_black + hispanic_black),
         overall_am_in_ak_native = sum(not_hispanic_am_in_ak_native + hispanic_am_in_ak_native),
         overall_asian_pi = sum(not_hispanic_asian_pi + hispanic_asian_pi),
         overall_male = sum(not_hispanic_white_male + not_hispanic_black_male + not_hispanic_am_in_ak_native_male + not_hispanic_asian_pi_male + hispanic_white_male + hispanic_black_male + hispanic_am_in_ak_native_male + hispanic_asian_pi_male),
         overall_female = sum(not_hispanic_white_female + not_hispanic_black_female + not_hispanic_am_in_ak_native_female + not_hispanic_asian_pi_female + hispanic_white_female + hispanic_black_female + hispanic_am_in_ak_native_female + hispanic_asian_pi_female),
         overall_8_17_population = sum(overall_male + overall_female)) %>% 
  dplyr::select(state,overall_8_17_population,overall_female,overall_male,hispanic_any_race,not_hispanic_asian_pi,not_hispanic_am_in_ak_native,not_hispanic_black,not_hispanic_white) %>% 
  ungroup()

### aggregate to state level
### combine race and sex columns into several new overall columns for race/ethnicity overall, race overall w/o ethnicity, and sex overall
df_acs_bridged_age_race_sex_15_19_final_state_aggregated_va <- df_acs_bridged_age_race_sex_15_19_wide %>%
  group_by(state) %>%
  summarize(not_hispanic_white = sum(not_hispanic_white_male + not_hispanic_white_female),
         not_hispanic_black = sum(not_hispanic_black_male + not_hispanic_black_female),
         not_hispanic_am_in_ak_native = sum(not_hispanic_am_in_ak_native_male + not_hispanic_am_in_ak_native_female),
         not_hispanic_asian_pi = sum(not_hispanic_asian_pi_male + not_hispanic_asian_pi_female),
         hispanic_white = sum(hispanic_white_male + hispanic_white_female),
         hispanic_black = sum(hispanic_black_male + hispanic_black_female),
         hispanic_am_in_ak_native = sum(hispanic_am_in_ak_native_male + hispanic_am_in_ak_native_female),
         hispanic_asian_pi = sum(hispanic_asian_pi_male + hispanic_asian_pi_female),
         hispanic_any_race = sum(hispanic_white + hispanic_black + hispanic_am_in_ak_native + hispanic_asian_pi),
         overall_white = sum(not_hispanic_white + hispanic_white),
         overall_black = sum(not_hispanic_black + hispanic_black),
         overall_am_in_ak_native = sum(not_hispanic_am_in_ak_native + hispanic_am_in_ak_native),
         overall_asian_pi = sum(not_hispanic_asian_pi + hispanic_asian_pi),
         overall_male = sum(not_hispanic_white_male + not_hispanic_black_male + not_hispanic_am_in_ak_native_male + not_hispanic_asian_pi_male + hispanic_white_male + hispanic_black_male + hispanic_am_in_ak_native_male + hispanic_asian_pi_male),
         overall_female = sum(not_hispanic_white_female + not_hispanic_black_female + not_hispanic_am_in_ak_native_female + not_hispanic_asian_pi_female + hispanic_white_female + hispanic_black_female + hispanic_am_in_ak_native_female + hispanic_asian_pi_female),
         overall_8_17_population = sum(overall_male + overall_female)) %>%
  dplyr::select(state,overall_8_17_population,overall_female,overall_male,hispanic_any_race,not_hispanic_asian_pi,not_hispanic_am_in_ak_native,not_hispanic_black,not_hispanic_white) %>%
  ungroup()


### pull in state + county fips lookup table to add county name to datafile via tidycensus function fips_codes
df_fips_lookup <- fips_codes %>% 
  filter(state_code == as.numeric(state_to_pull)) %>% ### this is where we filter on state
  mutate(co_fips = as.numeric(county_code)) %>% ### create co_fips for merge with df_acs_bridged_age_race_sex_15_19_final
  rename(county_name = county)

### left join fips_lookup and df_acs_bridged_age_race_sex_15_19_final (left joining df_acs_bridged_age_race_sex_15_19_final b/c there may be cases where a county is missing demographic acs data but we'd want to include the county name/fips code in the final file anyways; the lookup will have all counties regardless of missingness)
df_acs_bridged_age_race_sex_15_19_final <- left_join(df_fips_lookup, df_acs_bridged_age_race_sex_15_19_final, by = "co_fips")


### write out final file for incorporation into base juvenile population rate calculations

### set sharepoint path using csgjcr function
sharepoint_ojjdp_va_analysis_analytic_data <- csgjcr::csg_sp_path(file.path("JJ_OJJDP/Data/VA/analysis/analytic"))

write_rds(df_acs_bridged_age_race_sex_15_19_final_state_aggregated_va,
          file.path(sharepoint_ojjdp_va_analysis_analytic_data,"df_acs_bridged_age_race_sex_15_19_final_state_aggregated_va.rds"))

### write out df_acs_bridged_age_race_sex_15_19_final file for analysis
write_rds(df_acs_bridged_age_race_sex_15_19_final,
          file.path(sharepoint_ojjdp_va_analysis_analytic_data,"df_acs_bridged_age_race_sex_15_19_final_va.rds"))

In the following analysis, the outcome variable is binary – split into petitioned at intake (excluding court summons) and formally diverted (meaning complaint was diverted at intake). All records with other intake complaint decisions are excluded.
NOTE: I am currently running the regression on youth with no prior JJ history – also filtering on intakes labelled as either “Delinquent” or “Status” (we probably need to ask Nina why there are youth with no prior JJ history, but violations). Predictors included in preliminary model are:

race
gender
age at intake
CSU
referral/petitioner source
category of offense
year of petition
counts of felony, misdemeanor, status, and violation charges associated with intake/complaint

Another control we could add is something on how rural/urban each county is…

library(sjPlot)
library(sjmisc)
library(sjlabelled)
library(marginaleffects)

intake_complaints_no_prior_jj_to_model_diversion_petitioned <- df_analytic_complaints_disposition_caseload %>%
  filter(intake_decision_clean%in%c("Diverted","Petitioned"),
         jj_history_clean=="No Prior JJ History",
         flg_category%in%c("Deliquent","Status")) %>% 
  mutate(race = fct_relevel(race_clean, "White"),
         gender = fct_relevel(gender_clean, "Male"),
         referral_source_clean = fct_relevel(referral_source_clean, "Other"),
         date_opened_year = fct_relevel(as.character(date_opened_year), "2015"),
         intake_diverted_flag_num = ifelse(intake_diverted_flag=="Yes",
                                           1,0)) %>% 
  distinct(juvenile_number,
           .keep_all=TRUE)

va_diversion_petition_model <- glm(
  intake_diverted_flag_num ~ race + gender + intake_age + csu + referral_source_clean + dai +
    date_opened_year + count_misd_with_case + count_felony_with_case + count_status_with_case + count_violation_with_case,
  family = "binomial", 
  data = intake_complaints_no_prior_jj_to_model_diversion_petitioned)


tab_model(va_diversion_petition_model,
          p.style = "numeric_stars")

title: Analysis: Part I
section: Table 12. Model Output: Petition within One Year
text:
Table 12. Model Output: Petition within One Year
In the following analysis, the outcome variable is binary – whether a youth received a petitioned complaint within a year of their first intake (where the intake decision was diversion). All records with other intake complaint decisions are excluded from this analysis.
NOTE: I am currently running the regression on youth with no prior JJ history and who were initially diverted. I have removed the filter to only include intakes labelled as either “Delinquent” or “Status” so some charges are “other violation”, “Prob./Parole Violation”, and “court order violation (we probably want to ask Nina why there are youth with no prior JJ history, but violations).
Predictors included in model are:

race
gender
age at intake
CSU
referral/petitioner source
category of offense
year of petition
counts of felony, misdemeanor, status, and violation charges associated with intake/complaint

Another control we could add is something on how rural/urban each county is…

intake_initial_diversion_new_petition_within_a_year_model <- df_analytic_complaints_disposition_caseload %>%
  filter(jj_history_clean=="No Prior JJ History",
         intake_decision_clean=="Diverted",
         !is.na(intake_decision_regression_model_petition)==TRUE) %>% 
  mutate(race = fct_relevel(race_clean, "White"),
         gender = fct_relevel(gender_clean, "Male"),
         referral_source_clean = fct_relevel(referral_source_clean, "Other"),
         date_opened_year = fct_relevel(as.character(date_opened_year), "2015")) %>% 
  distinct(juvenile_number,
           .keep_all=TRUE)

va_diversion_new_petition_model <- glm(
  regression_outcome_new_petition_one_year_first_time_jj ~ race + gender + intake_age + csu + referral_source_clean + dai +
    date_opened_year + count_misd_with_case + count_felony_with_case + count_status_with_case + count_violation_with_case,
  family = "binomial", 
  data = intake_initial_diversion_new_petition_within_a_year_model)


tab_model(va_diversion_new_petition_model,
          p.style = "numeric_stars")
